provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 5 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: presta -> (absent from the aligned window); quesumus domine auxilium gratie tue -> quesunius d mine auxflium gr ti tuse; conuenienter -> conueui nter; hostibus -> h stibus; corporis -> c rporis per d minum alia; 1922 Mame text layer damages 4 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): presta -> uesta; quesumus domine -> queesumus p demine; gratie tue -> gratise tuze; orationibus -> oratidnibus; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 106, artifact PDF p. 220; the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Feria V post dominicam II in Quadragesima) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Oratio the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. The 1862's own locus for this day scores only 0.58 on a token-level alignment; every difference behind that score is recogniser damage (accents dropped, words split at line breaks, running heads and the scan's watermark intruding), not a different petition. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Praesta nobis, quaesumus, Domine, auxilium gratiae tuae: ut, jejuniis et
orationibus convenienter intenti, liberemur ab hostibus mentis et corporis.
Per Dominum.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Praesenti sacrificio, nomini tuo nos, Domine, jejunia dicata sanctificent:
ut, quod observantia nostra profitetur exterius, interius operetur effectu.
Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat
in unitate.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Gratia tua nos, quaesumus, Domine, non derelinquat: quae et sacrae nos
deditos faciat servituti, et tuam nobis opem semper acquirat. Per Dominum.
